A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reference Grounded Skill Discovery study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original humanoid simulation results for imitation quality, discovered skills and downstream goal reaching in Table 1 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation results and adds Meta-Motivo comparisons, additional goal-reaching conditions, diversity sensitivity results and measured motion-embedding alignment.

M1.justification: The contrastive pretraining, imitation reward, parallel discovery, encoder regularization and reference-state initialization remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2. The diversity sweep uses existing vMF sampling. The revised downstream task reward changes the evaluation protocol rather than RGSD itself.

E1.justification: The same 20 ACCAD motions, five motion categories and simulated SMPL humanoid are retained. Section 5.3 extends goal reaching from sidestepping alone to freestyle, sidestepping and backward conditions, a focused expansion of task requirements within the existing locomotion domain.

E2.justification: Meta-Motivo, previously discussed only as related work, becomes an evaluated comparator in imitation, discovered-skill and downstream comparisons: Table 1 and Figures 4–5. This expands all three central comparisons while retaining the previously evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 replaces squared goal-distance and squared Euclidean latent-distance reward terms with rescaled distance and cosine-distance terms, using coefficients 0.25 and 8; freestyle omits the style term. New protocols sweep kappa over 20, 100 and 1000 and measure embedding alignment across pretraining checkpoints. The existing 500-trajectory imitation evaluation remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds two substantive diagnostic analyses: sensitivity of behavioral diversity and FID to sampling concentration on three motions (Figure 6), and empirical within-motion alignment through training, including visualization and cosine-similarity measurements (Appendix E, Figure 7). The existing METRA failure analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 changes the stated downstream random-seed count from five to three. Appendix E newly reports alignment as 0.99998 ± 8.91e-6 across 20 motions, although it does not identify what the plus-minus quantity represents.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Meta-Motivo results while retaining existing scores: Meta-Motivo has lower FID than RGSD in all five categories, whereas RGSD has lower Cartesian error in all five. Figures 4–7 add comparator, diversity and alignment results. Downstream curves and FIDs are replaced under revised settings; for example, RGSD sidestepping FID changes from 34.3 to 6.8, which is not a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The vMF-to-InfoNCE derivation, within-motion alignment proof, reward-optimality proof and local quasi-concavity argument are retained from v1 Appendices A–C in v2 Appendices B–D. Equation numbering changes, but no substantive mathematical revision is evident. The new alignment study supplies empirical evidence.

C1.justification: The abstract refines the general downstream-control superiority claim into a more specific claim about satisfying user-specified locomotion styles that imitation baselines often fail to maintain. The central reference-grounding contribution, introduction's contribution list and conclusion remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explains downstream style preservation through discovering turning variants absent from the reference motions and extends the imitation-versus-discovery interpretation to Meta-Motivo. Appendix E newly discusses overlapping-state ambiguity, why phase and frame history mitigate it, and dependence of suitable history length on the dataset.

D1.justification: Figure 4 newly specifies 150 displayed trajectories per method. Appendix E documents the alignment calculation and visualization of the first three latent dimensions. A new reproducibility statement promises code release upon acceptance, without documenting an actual release. Existing algorithms, motion filenames, state specifications and Table 2 hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Blier et al. (2021) and Touati and Ollivier (2021) for forward–backward representations. Section 2.2 revises discussion of Meta-Motivo's GAIL connection and CALM's treatment of ASE mode collapse. The broader imitation-for-discovery positioning remains unchanged; Meta-Motivo was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect the abstract, introductory example, related work and experimental discussion, including removal of duplicated FID commentary. The METRA subsection becomes Section 6, and reproducibility and additional appendix sections are inserted. The method, theoretical narrative and overall progression remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a comparator row and Figure 4 a comparator column. Figure 5 expands from a small single-task curve to three panels with FID annotations. New Figures 6–7 display the diversity sweep and alignment progression. The earlier METRA figures are retained as Figures 8–9, rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: The added Meta-Motivo comparisons, downstream style conditions and latent-space analyses strengthen empirical support for RGSD's usefulness and grounding mechanism. These gains are tempered by fewer downstream seeds and inaccurate pairwise win-count summaries in Section 5.1: Table 1 supports five categories rather than the stated four. Revised downstream rewards also prevent interpreting the lower FIDs as same-setting improvements.
